Does the Fit Need a Rescue?

Source: R/mxHelper-needs-rescue.R
MxHelperNeedsRescue.Rd

Tests whether a model needs another fit: its status code is missing or not in ok_codes, it is not a good fit (MxHelperIsGoodFit()), its Hessian is not positive definite (MxHelperHasPdHessian()), or an estimate is at an actionable bound (MxHelperAtBounds()). When a test fails with an error, the answer is TRUE. The arguments are checked first; the internal version, without checks, is the one other projects copy.

Usage

MxHelperNeedsRescue(
  model,
  grad_tol = 0.01,
  ok_codes = 0L,
  require_finite_fit = TRUE,
  hess_tol_abs = 1e-08,
  hess_tol_rel = 1e-10,
  check_condition = TRUE,
  cond_max = 1e+12,
  abs_bnd_tol = 1e-06,
  rel_bnd_tol = 1e-04,
  allowed_bounds = NULL
)

Arguments

model

An OpenMx model (MxModel).

grad_tol

Positive number. Largest absolute gradient of a good fit.

ok_codes

Integer vector. OpenMx status codes accepted as converged.

require_finite_fit

Logical. If TRUE, a good fit needs a finite fit value.

hess_tol_abs

Positive number. Absolute tolerance on the smallest eigenvalue of the Hessian.

hess_tol_rel

Positive number. Tolerance on the smallest eigenvalue of the Hessian, relative to its largest absolute eigenvalue.

check_condition

Logical. If TRUE, the Hessian must also have a condition number of at most cond_max.

cond_max

Positive number. Largest condition number of the Hessian.

abs_bnd_tol

Positive number. Absolute tolerance for an estimate at a bound.

rel_bnd_tol

Positive number. Tolerance for an estimate at a bound, relative to the larger of the absolute estimate, the absolute bound, and 1.

allowed_bounds

List or NULL. Parameters allowed to rest at a bound: a list with the character vectors lower and upper of parameter labels. Their bound hits are reported but are not actionable.

Value

Returns TRUE or FALSE. The internal version returns TRUE when model is not an OpenMx model.

See also

Other Fit Diagnostics Functions: MxHelperHasPdHessian(), MxHelperIsGoodFit(), MxHelperStatusCode()

Author

Ivan Jacob Agaloos Pesigan

Examples

set.seed(seed = 42)
x <- data.frame(
  y1 = rnorm(n = 50),
  y2 = rnorm(n = 50)
)
fit <- MxHelperQuiet(
  expr = MxHelperMuSigma(
    x = x,
    extraTries = 2
  )
)
MxHelperNeedsRescue(
  model = fit
)
#> [1] FALSE
